sections.history: Tiruvedikudi lies near Tiruvaiyaru, about 7 km away on the Kaveri, in Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam: Tirugnana Sambandar venerated Vedapureeswarar in two padigams and Appar in two more, in the Tevaram. The shrine is the fourth of the celebrated Saptha Sthana (seven-place) temples of Tiruvaiyaru, whose festival links the seven villages. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian river-bank temple, the shrine enshrines Vedapureeswarar — also called Vazhai Madu Nathar — in the sanctum, with the goddess Mangayarkarasi in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The sanctum is noted for its reversed configuration, with the goddess to the right and the lord to the left. The temple keeps the form of the Shiva shrines of the Tiruvaiyaru belt.
sections.legends: The name Vedapureeswarar is bound to the legend of the Vedas, who by tradition undertook penance here upon Shiva to be made pure — 'the lord of the city of the Vedas.' The shrine's place in the Saptha Sthana festival of Tiruvaiyaru ties it to the seven Shiva villages carried in procession together. The goddess Mangayarkarasi, 'queen among women,' stands beside the lord.
sections.festivals: The temple observes the Saptha Sthana festival of Tiruvaiyaru in Chithirai, with the deities of the seven villages borne together, besides Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Tiruvaiyaru belt include Tiruvedikudi among the seven.
sections.experience: At Tiruvedikudi the pilgrim comes to the fourth of the seven Tiruvaiyaru shrines, on the Kaveri's bank. Before Vedapureeswarar and Mangayarkarasi, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the river country, and the memory of the Vedas who did penance here to be made pure.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvedikudi lies about 7 km from Tiruvaiyaru and roughly 11 km from Thanjavur, in Thanjavur district. Thanjavur is the nearest rail head; Tiruvaiyaru is the nearest town, with buses and taxis to the village.
